acceptance_scope: The first overhead sword animation and its delivered first-person arm asset only, using the user-approved iteration_04 motion. This is not acceptance of a full-body character, all possible poses, eight other clips, exact reference-video graphics, or game integration outside separately tested harnesses.
method: Independent direct tools.view_image inspection of actual final 1280x720 delivery PNGs, the source-versus-final 16-stage comparison, an overview assembled from all 94 actual delivery frames, six original-side images and six freshly reimported GLB opposite-side images. No surrogate reference or authored pose values were generated by this review.

scope.review_artifact_created: visual_all_94_frames_contact.webp is a contact-sheet overview assembled from the actual final frames for inspection only; it does not change the asset or animation.

resolved_findings.evidence: Final delivery frames 034 and 038 are empty of both weapons and arms. Frame 049 is also empty at follow-through. The large hanging hilt formerly visible at source 17.9s is absent. Frame 007 retains only the small low shield rim, consistent with source 17.45s.

At frame 040 the arm continues through the right boundary. At 042 and 043 it continues through the lower boundary as the hand moves toward low center. No exposed detached shoulder tube or inverted whole-arm silhouette was seen in these images or the 94-frame overview.

The continuous sleeve replaces the previous exposed cylindrical elbow opening. Original-side and freshly imported opposite-side renders remain visually connected through samples 008, 080, 084, 086, 091 and 092. No background-through elbow hole or separated sleeve ring is visible.

The obvious independent ball-shaped inserts from iteration_05 are gone. The arm now follows a continuous sleeve contour with a smooth bend. It remains a simplified leather sleeve rather than detailed anatomical skin.
Straps and buckles remain on the sleeve in the inspected original and freshly imported opposite-side poses. No detached floating strap is visible.

This maximum-bend sample was directly inspected from both side directions, including the fresh GLB import. The sleeve stays continuous without a large tear, open elbow ring, loose insert or detached strap.

The shoulder-side terminal is now a filled end surface in the external views rather than a visible hollow cylinder. It remains an isolated capped arm end and is not attached to a rendered torso. That distinction is outside the accepted first-person arm scope.

reference_stage_checks.observation: Right-side ready/preparation and rising out of view remain consistent with the approved overhead direction. The small shield rim persists at frame 007.
Both weapons absent at the sampled hold times.
Fast high-right to low-center strike, right-to-bottom arm entry and disappearance after the pass are retained. The long guard's visible extra prong differs from the source asset.

Shield is present before sword at the specified sampled recovery stage; sword tip returns with a left lean and rises to the right-side ready state. This is not a claim that every onset frame exactly matches the source.

documented_nonblocking_residuals.observation: Small angular cuff/glove overlap lines and dark creases remain, notably around the inner wrist in final frame 040/042 and the upper wrist near side sample 092. The opposite-side reimport images show overlapping material/fold edges rather than a confirmed background-through opening or floating component.
documented_nonblocking_residuals.classification: Cosmetic residual within this first-person scope; no additional blocking surface repair identified from the inspected images.

documented_nonblocking_residuals.observation: The 94-frame overview shows a gradual shield return before the specified 18.5s sample. A direct comparison at source 18.4s (frame 1104 / final relative frame 064) shows the final shield noticeably higher in view, while the source has at most a minute rim at the very bottom. Source frame 1097 at 18.283333s is still visually empty.
documented_nonblocking_residuals.classification: Residual timing/projection difference in the user-approved preserved iteration_04 motion, not a new skinning or surface regression. Acceptance does not mean exact source-frame reproduction. No change to the accepted motion was made by this review.

documented_nonblocking_residuals.observation: The intentionally long handle/pommel extends much farther beneath the fist than the reference's compact handle. During the cut, one long guard arm projects beside the blade; during recovery the guard spans more of the lower frame.
documented_nonblocking_residuals.classification: Known weapon-design difference; the user's approved long handle is preserved.

documented_nonblocking_residuals.observation: The brown glove/leather sleeve, wooden shield, textured blade and neutral studio background differ from the reference's grey mannequin and environment. The sleeve surface is smooth and simplified, and the capped shoulder is not a full-body character connection.
documented_nonblocking_residuals.classification: Known visual and asset-scope limitations; no claim of photorealistic anatomy or full-body completion.

supporting_numeric_evidence_read.method_reported: Separate actual Blender dependency-graph evaluation of saved blend and freshly imported GLB at all 187 original 120Hz sample times; evaluated vertices compared both ways using bind-position correspondence and bind-corrected bone matrices.
supporting_numeric_evidence_read.important_runtime_contract: Use the delivered skin, bind transforms and bone animation. Applying only right_arm.parts_camera omits the continuous sleeve deformation.
supporting_numeric_evidence_read.reviewer_limit: This existing report was read and its outcome recorded; the numeric audit was not rerun here. Separate Godot execution claims belong to the responsible validation report.

conclusion: Accept the delivered iteration_07 first-person overhead arm asset with the residuals listed above. The inspected critical frames and both side directions show the requested arm-surface repairs, including the strongest bend and the previous offscreen hold failure. The single overhead scope is closed for this visual review; no other animation, full-body model or exact-reference-equivalence acceptance is implied.
